summary: Tent camp and platform tower dated 1915 by the register and 1916 by other sources; later abandoned; Willhiteweb found faint trail and rock work but no relics.

facts.design: Tent camp with a platform tower
facts.status_note: Register says the site is gone; sources describe it as abandoned, with no standing structure
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service (Mount Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest)

visit.trail_note: No simple route to the summit; old miners trails reach the northern ridges about halfway; Willhiteweb describes a short class 4 rock section on the approach; road access is fair gravel

events.note: Register gives 1915 as the built year: a tent and platform tower on the site
Camp moved over to Jumbo the year after the 1915 Gold Mountain start (Willhiteweb); Washington Lookouts dates the establishment to 1916
Registered April 3, 2020; nominated by Tammy McLeod

evidence.supports: tent and platform tower on the site in 1915
evidence.quote: In 1915 there was a tent and platform tower on the site.
It was later abandoned and is gone.

evidence.supports: firelookout.com says camp and platform tower, then abandoned

evidence.quote: 1916: The lookout was established with a rock platform and a tent camp. The duties were transferred from the Gold Hill lookout.

evidence.supports: listing marks the site as removed
camp moved to Jumbo the year after 1915
evidence.quote: The following year, the lookout camp was moved over to Jumbo Mountain, specifically the north summit.
The first lookout man was Rowland Atchson, who was also the first lookout man on Gold Hill in 1915.

evidence.supports: no simple route to the summit
evidence.quote: There is no simple way to reach the summit although miners trails skirted up the northern ridges of the mountain about halfway.

evidence.supports: possibly hardest former lookout to reach in Washington
evidence.quote: The Jumbo Mountain Lookout site might be the hardest to reach of all the former lookouts in Washington.

evidence.supports: faint trail signs and rock work on the summit
evidence.quote: there were faint signs of a trail in the summit rocks as well as some rock work

evidence.supports: Gold Mountain camp first used in 1915; camp moved to Jumbo the following year
evidence.quote: According to history buffs in Darrington, the Gold Mountain lookout camp was the first to be used in the Darrington District, in 1915.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register says 1915 (tent and platform tower). Willhiteweb says the Gold Mountain camp began in 1915 and moved to Jumbo the following year; Washington Lookouts dates the Jumbo establishment to 1916. The story reports both dates.
Willhiteweb names Gold Mountain and Washington Lookouts names Gold Hill as the lookout whose duties moved to Jumbo. The story does not name it.

notes_for_editor: Brief 1915 built and 2020 FFLOS registration are confirmed by the register, but 1916 is the year other sources give for the move to Jumbo; the 1915 event is kept with the conflict noted. Access level is omitted because no source gives an official access status. The neighboring lookout is named Gold Mountain by Willhiteweb and Gold Hill by Washington Lookouts. No date is given for the abandonment, so no abandoned event is recorded.
